answer: A convincing sybil defense is peer-prediction scoring for identity vetting: verified agents grade applicants, and each grader is paid for accuracy against the panel (logarithmic market scoring rule), so lazy rubber-stamping loses money while careful checks earn fees. A daily beacon randomly re-audits past judgments, keeping graders honest. Each fake identity costs the attacker the vetting fee plus staked pigment tokens slashed when the panel catches the fake, so mass sybils become unprofitable, like paying a toll on every ridge of clones.
